Harvest Minerals Limited
("Harvest" or the "Company")
Technical Cooperation Agreement with Brazilian Geological Survey
for Strategic Minerals and Rare Earths
Harvest Minerals Limited ("Harvest" or the "Company") the AIM listed resource company, has entered into a Technical-Scientific Cooperation Agreement with Serviço Geológico do Brasil ("SGB"), the Brazilian Geological Survey and the country's leading geoscience institution, to research the potential occurrence of mineral commodities considered critical or strategic for Brazil (the "Agreement").
Overview:
·
Harvest has a portfolio of highly prospective ionic adsorption clay ("IAC") rare earth element ("REE") projects across Brazil, one of the world's most prospective jurisdictions for clay-hosted rare earth mineralisation.
·
SGB has a strategic mandate to advance Brazil's geological knowledge of critical and strategic minerals, including rare earth elements, and to identify prospective areas capable of supporting future mineral investment and development.
·
The Agreement, signed with Harvest's subsidiary Scanty Mineração Ltda ("Scanty"), will focus primarily on the REE potential of the Capão Bonito, Carambeí, Cerro Azul and Sguário Granite project areas, located within the Ribeira Belt in the states of São Paulo and Paraná.
·
Previous work, including extensive geological evaluation and technical studies, has demonstrated the potential of the project areas, with results including a peak grade of 5,662 ppm TREO and mineralised intercepts of up to 17 m in thickness, providing a strong technical foundation now recognised by both parties.
·
Partnership formally positions Harvest, through Scanty, within Brazil's national critical minerals agenda and provides institutional validation by the federal geological agency of its exploration targets and REE mineralisation model hosted within the alkaline granites of the Ribeira Belt.
·
24 months agreement, which starts immediately and has a robust technical scope including advanced chemical and mineralogical characterisation, laboratory-scale REE extraction and recovery test work.
o
For work requested by SGB, Harvest shall incur no cost and will have access to the data/results.
Brian McMaster, Chairman of Harvest, said:
"We are extremely excited to be partnering with the Brazilian Geological Survey at a time when securing domestic supplies of critical minerals, particularly REEs, is becoming an increasingly important strategic priority for Brazil. Importantly, SGB's decision to work with Harvest reflects its recognition of the geological potential of our licences and brings the country's leading geoscience institution alongside us to evaluate what we believe is a highly prospective portfolio of REE projects in the Ribeira Belt.
"Brazil has the geological potential to become an important source of the critical minerals required by modern industries, and we are delighted that Harvest can play a role in that ambition. With encouraging results already generated across our licences, including grades of up to 5,662 ppm TREO and mineralised intercepts of up to 17 metres, we believe there is a compelling foundation for this work. This 24-month programme will allow us to build on that potential alongside a federal government partner, advance our geological and metallurgical understanding, and contribute to Brazil's objective of developing secure domestic sources of strategically important Rare Earth Elements."
Project Scope:
The project, entitled
"Study of the Rare Earth Elements (REE) potential in the Ribeira Belt - SP, PR, SC"
, will cover the following areas of Scanty's active portfolio also known as the Southeast Hub (RNS 1.09.26):
●
Capão Bonito Granite (SP):
Scanty's main project up to date. Features
76 auger holes
completed (839 m), with a peak of
5,662 ppm TREO
and intercepts of up to
17 m
in thickness. The ionic adsorption clay (IAC) character was supported by ammonium sulphate leaching testwork (AMSUL leach).
●
Sguário Granite (SP):
Reports a historical peak of
2,796 ppm TREO
and mineralisation open at depth. A first-pass reconnaissance campaign of
13 holes (152 m)
was completed during 2025, with assay results pending.
●
Carambeí Granite (PR):
Comprising four exploration licences. A first-pass reconnaissance drilling programme of
13 auger holes (138 m)
was completed in 2025, with assay results pending.
●
Cerro Azul Granite (PR):
Comprising five exploration licences. Following initial desktop review, a first-pass reconnaissance programme of
6 auger holes (99 m)
was completed in 2025, with assay results pending.
The activities planned under the 24-month joint work programme comprise multiple workstreams designed to significantly enhance the understanding of the REE potential across the project areas, including:
● Detailed studies of weathering alteration profiles and correlation with mineralising processes related to REE enrichment.
● Chemical and mineralogical characterisation of rock, saprolite and soil samples using X-ray fluorescence (XRF), inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), reflectance spectroscopy (RS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and automated mineralogy.
● Laboratory-scale REE extraction and recovery testwork using different leach solutions (acidic, saline and complexing), including optimisation of parameters such as pH, temperature, particle size and contact time.
● Mutual sharing of surface and drill core samples belonging to the participating institutions for academic and industrial research purposes.
Strategic Significance:
The partnership with the SGB positions Harvest, via Scanty, in line with the national critical minerals policy and provides independent validation of the REE mineralisation model hosted by the alkaline granites of the Ribeira Belt. This is the same ionic adsorption clay model underpinning the advancement of the Capão Bonito project. The characterisation studies and leaching test work will provide crucial scientific input to the geological and metallurgical understanding of the targets, with potential for high-impact publications in the mineral sector.
Brazil has identified critical and strategic minerals, including rare earth elements, as an important national priority, with a focus on strengthening domestic supply chains, expanding geological knowledge and supporting the development of mineral resources essential to advanced technologies, the energy transition and industrial development. Harvest's cooperation with SGB aligns the Company directly with this national agenda and provides an opportunity for its REE projects to benefit from the technical expertise and institutional involvement of Brazil's federal geological agency, while contributing to the country's broader objective of identifying and developing secure domestic sources of strategically important minerals.
Next Steps:
Execution of the 24 month work programme will commence immediately with the exchange of samples between the parties, followed by laboratory characterisation campaigns. The Company will keep the market duly informed of the results of the activities and any discoveries arising from this technical cooperation.
Qualified Persons Statement:
The technical information in this announcement is based on data compiled and reviewed by Celeste Queiroz, consulting geologist for Harvest Minerals Limited. Celeste Queiroz is a Fellow of the Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy (AusIMM) and a Registered Qualified Professional at CBRR (Comissão Brasileira de Recursos e Reservas) and has sufficient experience relevant to the style of mineralisation and type of deposit under consideration to qualify as a Competent Person as defined in the 2012 Edition of the "Australasian Code for Reporting of Exploration Results, Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves" (JORC).

latest.title: Completed acquisition of Scanty Mineracao & TVR
latest.content:
Today 08:30

Harvest Minerals Limited / Index: LSE / Epic: HMI / Sector: Mining
1 September 2026
Harvest Minerals Limited ("Harvest" or the "Company")
Completion of acquisition of Scanty Mineracao and TVR
Overview on Newly Acquired Brazilian Rare Earth Portfolio and
Outline Exploration Roadmap
Harvest Minerals Limited ("Harvest" or the "Company") is pleased to announce, further to its 21 July 2026 announcement, that it has now completed the acquisition of Scanty Mineração Ltda. ("Scanty"), holders of a portfolio of highly prospective ionic adsorption clay ("IAC") rare earth element ("REE") projects. The acquisition, which complements the existing Arapua Rare Earth Project, establishes Harvest as an emerging rare earth exploration company with a portfolio of REE projects across Brazil, one of the world's most prospective jurisdictions for clay-hosted rare earth mineralisation, in addition to the Company's Brazilian fertilizer operations.
OVERVIEW
§
Strategic Acquisition:
Completion of the acquisition of Scanty adds a portfolio of eight multistage REE projects across four Brazilian states targeting IAC mineralisation.
§
Established Technical Foundation:
Prior to Harvest's acquisition, the projects benefited from several years of geological evaluation and technical work, including 98 auger holes totalling approximately 1,477 metres completed since 2024.
All the data sets are currently being reviewed and validated.
§
Pending Analytical Programme:
386 samples collected by Scanty at the Capão Bonito Project are being laboratory tested and results are expected at the end of the current quarter. This data will be incorporated into Harvest's geological interpretation to support planning of the next phase of exploration.
§
Historical leach testwork
: Historical testwork has already confirmed that mineralisation exhibits ionic adsorption clay behaviour, which provides strong encouragement for continued project advancement.
§
2026 Exploration Programme:
Following review of the historical dataset and receipt of the outstanding analytical results, Harvest intends to design and implement, subject to securing the necessary funding, a follow-up drilling programme at Capão Bonito to further evaluate its potential for future resource definition.
Brian McMaster, Chairman of Harvest, commented:
"The completion of the acquisition of Scanty represents a significant milestone in Harvest's strategy of building a meaningful rare earth business in Brazil. Rather than acquiring a single exploration project, we have assembled a broad portfolio that combines an advanced lead asset with multiple regional exploration opportunities capable of delivering long-term value.
"Capão Bonito immediately stood out as the cornerstone of the portfolio. The volume of work already by the previous operator, including drilling, metallurgy and geological interpretation, provides us with an excellent technical foundation from which to accelerate project advancement. Just as importantly, the project still has considerable room for growth as we continue to increase drill density, receive outstanding assay results and better understand the controls on rare earth recovery.
"While Capão Bonito will be our immediate priority, we are equally encouraged by the broader Southeast Hub. Several projects have now completed their first reconnaissance drilling programmes, and the pending analytical results have the potential to significantly expand the known mineralised footprint of the district and identify additional priority targets for follow-up exploration.
"Our objective over the coming 12 months is clear: systematically advance Capão Bonito towards potential initial Mineral Resource Estimate while continuing to unlock value across the remainder of the portfolio through disciplined targeted exploration and technical evaluation."
FURTHER INFORMATION
Building a Brazilian Rare Earth Platform
The acquisition of Scanty represents a transformational step in Harvest's evolution as a critical minerals' exploration company.
Since announcing its Technical Cooperation Agreement with Union Star Metals Limited (then called PVW Resources Limited) to evaluate the rare earth potential of the Arapua Project, Harvest has progressively expanded its understanding of the opportunity presented by ionic adsorption clay hosted rare earth mineralisation in Brazil. The acquisition of Scanty significantly accelerates this strategy by adding a diversified portfolio of exploration projects that have already benefited from several years of geological evaluation and technical work.
The portfolio comprises eight exploration projects located across the states of São Paulo, Paraná, Minas Gerais and Bahia. Together they provide Harvest with exposure to multiple prospective geological terrains while significantly increasing the Company's exploration footprint.
Unlike many early-stage exploration portfolios, the acquired assets are not all at the same stage of development. Instead, they provide a balanced pipeline ranging from regional target generation through to advanced drill-ready projects, where exploration has already established encouraging geological and metallurgical characteristics.
This diversified approach allows Harvest to pursue two complementary objectives simultaneously: advancing Capão Bonito towards an initial mineral resource while continuing to evaluate numerous additional exploration opportunities capable of delivering future discoveries.
The Company believes this strategy provides a balanced allocation of exploration capital, combining near-term development milestones with longer-term district-scale discovery potential.
The Portfolio
While each project is at a different stage of exploration, the portfolio was assembled by the previous operator based on favourable geological characteristics, weathered granitic terrains and the potential to host near-surface clay-hosted rare earth mineralisation.
The projects are grouped into two principal exploration regions:
·
Southeast Hub
- comprising Capão Bonito, Itapeva, Sguario, Carambeí and Cerro Azul. This represents the Company's immediate exploration focus, with the greatest amount of geological information and drilling completed to date.
·
Northeast Hub
- comprising earlier-stage regional projects in Ceará, Minas Gerais and Bahia States where reconnaissance work and target evaluation will continue in parallel with activities in the Southeast Hub.
Located within favourable granitic terrains extending across São Paulo and Paraná States, the Southeast Hub contains five projects sharing similar geological characteristics and exploration models. Although each project is at a different level of advancement, collectively they provide the opportunity to develop a district-scale rare earth business rather than a single isolated deposit.
Across the five projects, a total of 821 samples were collected and are currently undergoing laboratory analysis ahead of results this quarter. These results are expected to represent one of the most important value inflection points for the portfolio, as they will not only define the next stage of work at Capão Bonito but will also determine the exploration priorities for the remainder of the Southeast Hub.
Capão Bonito has been identified as Harvest's lead development asset and will be the primary focus of exploration activities during the next phase of work as it possesses by far the most advanced technical database, combining historical drilling, encouraging metallurgy and a more detailed understanding of the geological controls on mineralisation. It has progressed beyond initial target generation and, under Harvest's stewardship, will now enter the next phase of exploration with the objective of evaluating its potential for future resource definition.
Scanty has completed an auger drilling program at the Capão Bonito target, comprising 98 holes with a cumulative depth of approximately 1,477 metres. The average hole depth was 19 metres, with a maximum depth of 30 metres. Of the samples collected during the previous program, 386 individual samples remain pending laboratory analysis, with results expected later this quarter.
Historical leach testwork executed by Scanty confirmed that mineralisation exhibits ionic adsorption clay behaviour, which provide strong encouragement for continued project advancement.
The existing dataset provides a strong understanding of the geometry of the mineralised clay profile, establishing a solid foundation for the next phase of resource definition drilling.
Next Exploration Priorities
The immediate priority for 2026 is the completion of chemical analyses for the 386 samples collected at Capão Bonito during the 2025 drilling programme executed by the prior owner. These results are expected to expand the geological database, refine the geological interpretation of the project and identify the highest-priority areas for future drilling. Selected mineralised intervals will subsequently undergo desorption testing (ICM694) to further evaluate metallurgical performance.
Building Long-Term Value
Collectively, these workstreams are expected to advance the technical understanding of Capão Bonito while continuing to evaluate the broader exploration potential of the Southeast Hub. The programme, to be budgeted and detailed in due course, will be designed to support the next phase of exploration at Capão Bonito while advancing regional exploration across the portfolio, with the objective of further assessing the potential for future resource definition and identifying additional exploration opportunities.
Further details on the acquisition of Scanty
All conditions precedent have now been satisfied and therefore the acquisition of Scanty has now completed. Accordingly, the completion payments of A$200,000 in cash, and the issue of 40 million new Harvest ordinary shares have been triggered. Please refer to the Company's 21 July 2026 RNS for details on the further contingent consideration payable.
Admission to AIM and TVR
Application will be made to the London Stock Exchange for the above 40,000,000 new Ordinary Shares to be admitted to trading on AIM. It is expected that admission will become effective and that dealings in the new Ordinary Shares will commence at 8.00 a.m. on 2 September 2026 ("Admission").
Following the issue of such shares, the total issued share capital of the Company will consist of 543,169,217 Ordinary Shares with voting rights. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in treasury and accordingly there are no voting rights in respect of any treasury shares.
On Admission, the abovementioned figure of 543,169,217 Ordinary Shares may be used by shareholders in the Company as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, Harvest under the Financial Conduct Authority's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

latest.title: Acquisition of Brazilian Rare Earth Portfolio
latest.content:
Today 07:26
RNS Number : 1916N
Harvest Minerals Limited
21 July 2026
21 July 2026
Harvest Minerals Limited
("Harvest" or the "Company")
Acquisition of Brazilian Rare Earth Portfolio
Eight highly prospective ionic clay REE projects across key regions of Brazil
Harvest Minerals Limited (AIM: HMI), the AIM-listed Brazilian fertiliser producer and mineral development company, is pleased to announce that it has entered into a binding agreement to acquire 100% of Scanty Mineração Ltda ("Scanty"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Union Star Metals Limited (ASX: USM), in a cash, shares and milestone related transaction (the "Acquisition").
OVERVIEW
·
Scanty holds a portfolio of eight highly prospective ionic clay rare earth ("REE") projects across 27 exploration tenements in Brazil.
·
Projects include the Capão Bonito and Sguario projects, where geology is considered highly prospective for ionic clay-hosted REE mineralisation.
·
The Acquisition consideration is structured as to:
o
A$200,000 cash payment, and the issue of 40,000,00fa0 new Harvest ordinary shares, on completion
o
Up to a further A$300,000 cash payment for meeting development milestones;
o
The assumption of approximately A$1.5 million of deferred acquisition payments and associated 1.5% royalty obligations due to the previous vendors (see below).
·
Brazil is an emerging global REE jurisdiction, with favourable geology and a growing pipeline of advanced rare earth projects.
·
Builds on Harvest's initial opportunity at the Arapua REE Project in Brazil and leverages its established operating platform and technical expertise in Brazil to build a broader portfolio of highly prospective REE assets.
Brian McMaster, Executive Chairman, commented:
"This Acquisition marks the next step in Harvest's expanded critical minerals strategy and provides exposure to multiple high-quality assets. Building on the encouraging REE results at Arapua, we are leveraging our established operating platform and technical expertise in Brazil to build a broader portfolio of REE assets, within a structure that aligns consideration with project success, while maintaining capital discipline.
"Brazil's rare earth sector is attracting strong investor interest due to its potential to deliver large-scale, low-cost ionic clay deposits outside China, supported by favourable geology, established infrastructure, and a growing pipeline of advanced projects. We believe the Scanty tenements provide a strong platform for resource growth and long-term shareholder value creation."
DETAILS
Under the terms of the agreement, Harvest will acquire 100% of Scanty Mineração Ltda from Union Star Metals, adding eight REE projects to complement its existing portfolio. The Acquisition builds on encouraging REE results from Harvest's 100%-owned Arapuá Project, where work undertaken last year returned average Total Rare Earth Oxide ("TREO") concentrations ranging from 2,110.53 ppm to 2,656.99 ppm and confirmed the presence of REE mineralisation within the "Bone" lithotype.
Scanty's portfolio targets both ionic clay-hosted and hard rock rare earth mineralisation across the Cerro Azul, Capão Bonito, Itapeva, Sguario, Mucambo and Guaratinga project areas. The projects are located within established mineral provinces, including the Poços de Caldas Alkaline Complex and the Bahia Rare Earth Province, which host numerous rare earth, niobium, phosphate and bauxite deposits and are recognised as important centres for rare earth exploration in Brazil.
The most advanced assets are the Capão Bonito and Sguario projects, where fieldwork, including portable X-ray fluorescence ("pXRF") testing, has identified anomalous rare earth mineralisation at surface. Both projects are hosted within the Ribeira Orogeny and are associated with fractionated A-type granites, geological settings recognised as favourable for ionic clay-hosted rare earth mineralisation. Follow-up exploration will focus on validating historical work and advancing priority targets.
In addition, Brazil more widely offers highly prospective geology for ionic rare earth elements (REEs), with a growing pipeline of advanced-stage projects. Emerging producers are rapidly positioning the country as a key player in the global shift toward diversified, secure, and non-China-dominated REE supply chains.
The consideration comprises:
·
Initial cash payment of A$200,000, on completion.
·
Issue of 40,000,000 new ordinary shares in Harvest to Union Star Metals, on completion.
·
Deferred cash payment of A$100,000 upon declaration of a qualifying Mineral Resource with minimum content of 20Mt at 1,000ppm REO for the Project.
·
Deferred cash payment of A$200,000 upon achievement of the first development milestone (Pilot Plant, PEA or PFS), or after 60 months if not previously achieved.
·
Harvest will assume approximately A$1.5 million of deferred acquisition payments, to be satisfied in cash and/or Harvest shares (at the discretion of the Company) (subject to satisfaction of the vesting conditions as set out below), and associated 1.5% net smelter return royalty obligations, payable to the original vendors under a novation deed to be entered into.
o
For the AS$1.5 million to become payable, Harvest will need to have:
§
Defined and reported an inferred mineral resource of not less than 20 million tonnes at 1,000 ppm rare earth oxides, within 36 months of completion; and
§
Completed and reported a Scoping Study, which recommends a PFS to be undertaken, within 48 months of completion.
Related party transaction
Brian McMaster and Luis Azevedo, directors and substantial shareholders of the Company, comprised two of the four original vendors, then holding a combined 50% interest (25% each) in Scanty. The assumption of the deferred acquisition payments to Mr McMaster and Mr Azevedo by Harvest therefore constitutes a related party transaction pursuant to the AIM Rules. Mr Azevedo also is party to the royalty agreement. In this context, the Directors other than Mr McMaster and Mr Azevedo consider, having consulted with the Company's nominated adviser, Strand Hanson Limited, that the terms of such assumption of obligations are fair and reasonable insofar as its shareholders are concerned.
Schedule Four Disclosure
As at 31 December 2025, Scanty reported gross assets of approximately A$30k, with a loss before tax of approximately A$800k.
Completion of the Acquisition remains subject to certain customary conditions precedent, including Brazilian regulatory approval. Further announcements will be made as and when appropriate.

company_30s.what_they_do: HMI Ltd is a mining and materials company that focuses on extracting and processing rare‑earth elements.  The core business is to supply high‑purity rare‑earth metals for electronics, defense, and green‑energy applications.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Rare‑earth metals are essential for batteries, wind turbines, and advanced electronics.  The global shift to clean tech and the scarcity of these elements give HMI a strategic niche, especially as major producers face supply constraints.
company_30s.current_state: The company has recently gone through a series of board changes and has announced a new acquisition of a Brazilian rare‑earth portfolio.  It is still working on turning its operations profitable, with cash burn on the back burner while it seeks new contracts and capital injections.

rns_narrative: The company closed 2025 with a final results report that showed modest revenue growth but still negative cash flow.  A board change in March 2026 signals a shift in strategy, while the July acquisition of a Brazilian portfolio is a clear step toward expanding production capacity.

The narrative is a mix of consolidation and expansion: the company is trying to shore up its asset base and bring new projects online, but it remains cash‑constrained and still needs to demonstrate profitability.
These moves suggest the firm is stabilising its operations and positioning itself for a potential turnaround, especially if the new assets start generating revenue.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Silent scepticism with a flicker of optimism from a few large‑volume traders.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders point to the 9‑million‑share buy on July 22 as a sign that smart money is already piling in, hoping the acquisition will unlock value.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Many voices warn that the company still has a long way to go to become profitable, citing the recent board shake‑up as a sign of instability and the lack of a clear earnings turnaround plan.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter is still weak and fragmented.  A few bullish posts appear after the acquisition announcement, but overall the mood is cautious, with most community members waiting for a clear earnings beat before committing.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Search interest for the ticker is flat; there is no recent spike in Google Trends, which means the market is largely unaware of any upcoming event.

near_term_catalysts: The July 21 acquisition announcement could drive a price jump if the new assets are expected to generate cash flow soon.
If the company releases a Q3 earnings report that shows improved margins or a positive cash‑flow forecast, that would be a strong trigger.
A rise in global rare‑earth prices or a new contract with a major OEM would also support a rebound.
Volume spikes above the 20‑day average combined with a break above the 52‑week low would confirm a bounce.
